More evidence suggesting faces are processed holistically was reported by Richler et al . (2011) using composite faces . Composite faces consist of a top half and a bottom half which may or may not be of the same face . The participants decided whether the top halves of two successive composite faces were the same or different . Performance was worse when the bottom halves of the two composite faces were different . This composite face effect suggests that people are unable to ignore the bottom halves and thus that processing of the composite faces is holistic .
An area that is associated with face processing; the term is somewhat misleading given that the area is also associated with processing other categories of objects .
Representations (e . g . , visual images) resembling pictures in that objects within them are organised spatially .
Within Kosslyn ' s theory , a short -term visual memory store .
When two different visual stimuli are presented one to each eye , only one stimulus is seen; the seen stimulus alternates over time .
The changing patterns of light on the retina produced by movement of the observer relative to the environment as well as by eye and head movements .
An internal copy of a motor command (e . g . , to the eyes); it can be used to compare actual with desired movement .
Neurons that respond to actions whether performed by oneself or someone else; it is claimed these neurons assist in imitating and understanding others ’ actions .

A situation in which individuals try to attend to only one source of information while ignoring other stimuli; also known as selective attention .
A situation in which two tasks are performed at the same time; also known as multitasking .

Suppose we present participants with two streams of lights (as was done by Eimer and Schröger (1998)) , with one stream of lights being presented to the left and the other to the right . In one condition , participants detect deviant visual events (e . g . , longer than usual stimuli) presented to one side only . In the other condition , participants detect deviant auditory events in only one stream .
Attention to a given spatial location determined by " automatic " processes .

Stored units formed from integrating smaller pieces of information .
A modality-free , limited capacity , component of working memory .

A component of working memory used to process visual and spatial information and to store this information briefly .
A component of working memory; it is essentially passive and stores integrated information briefly .
Rapid repetition of a simple sound (e . g . , “ the the the ” ) , w hich uses the articulatory control process of the phonological loop .

An assessment of how much information can be processed and stored at the same time; individuals with high capacity have higher intelligence and more attentional control .
The largest number of sentences read for comprehension from which an individual can recall all the final words over 50% of the time .
The maximum number of items (arithmetical questions + words) for which an individual can recall all the words more than 50% of the time .
The ability to use knowledge , skills and experience .
Learning complex information without conscious awareness of what has been learned .

Vivid and detailed memories of dramatic events (e . g . , 9/11) .
An exceptional ability to remember the events of one ’ s own life .

The process of translating a word ’ s meaning into its sound representation during speech production .
Severe problems in the comprehension and/or production of language caused by brain damage .
A form of aphasia involving non-fluent speech and grammatical errors .
A form of aphasia involving fluent speech with many content words missing and impaired comprehension .
A condition caused by brain damage in which there is an impaired ability to name objects .
A store in which graphemic information about the individual letters in a word is held immediately prior to spelling the word .
A condition caused by brain damage in which familiar words can be spelled reasonably well but non-words cannot .
A condition caused by brain damage in which there is poor spelling of irregular words , reasonable spelling of regular words and some success in spelling non-words .
A stage of problem solving in which the problem is put to one side for some time; it is claimed to facilitate problem solving .
The inflexible focus on the usual function(s) of an object in problem solving .

An abstract description of all the possible states that can occur within a given problem .

A simple heuristic used by problem solvers in which they focus on making moves that will apparently put them closer to the goal .
A heuristic or rule of thumb in which slow progress towards problem solution triggers a change of strategy .
Someone who is economical with their time and effort when performing a thinking task .
This form of practice involves the learner being provided with informative feedback and having the chance to correct his/her errors .
Used by experts to store relevant information rapidly in long-term memory and to access it through retrieval cues in working memory .

The relative frequency of an event within a given population .
The assumption that an object or individual belongs to a specified category because it is representative (typical) of that category .
The mistaken assumption that the probability of a conjunction of two events is greater than the probability of one of them .
The rule of thumb that the frequencies of events can be estimated accurately by the subjective ease with which they can be retrieved .
Using one ’ s emotional responses to influence rapid judgements or decisions .
Using the knowledge that only one out of two objects is recognised as the basis for making a judgement .

The greater sensitivity to potential losses than potential gains shown by most people engaged in decision making .

A rule of thumb used by scientists in which unexpected findings are used to develop new hypotheses and lines of research .

In informal reasoning , the tendency to evaluate statements in terms of one ' s own beliefs or to generate reasons or arguments supporting those beliefs .
The claim that an innocuous first step will lead to an undesirable outcome; sometimes regarded as a fallacy .

A part of the brain strongly associated with several emotions including fear; it is located towards the front of the temporal lobe .

Support for the “ do - it - yourself principle ” was obtained by Eich and Metcalfe (1989) . At learning , participants were assigned to read (e . g . , river - valley) or generate (e . g . , river - v \_\_\_\_ ) conditions . In the generate condition , they completed the second word in each pair during learning and so engaged in effortful processing . The mood - state - dependent effect was four times greater in the generate condition .
